precise_scope: For every connected smooth compact Kahler n-fold, pseudoeffective zero-volume class and actual reference type, degree-d relative full mass and joint-linear integrability define common auxiliary-independent domains. Bare mixed product currents are continuous under decreasing full-mass sequences with full-mass limits. The bounded-family kernel in the actual span of Kahler complementary powers extends unchanged to the whole common domain, giving a quantified minimum operator-data quotient with raw mass, same-type anchor and theta-gauge invariance. A P1 x P1 example computes its geometric kernel and infinite dimension. Rescaled perturbations converge for decreasing original-background full-mass paths with convergent classes and complementary-power quotient data; a same-class alternating-form path has distinct limits. Original P15.2 is not solved.
limitations: No intrinsic geometric d-dimensional carrier is constructed: all output measures have carrier X of dimension n, and W/N is reference data only.
No independently geometric general classification of the operator kernel or universal minimum reference for every possible zero-volume theory is proved.

Perturbation independence retains original-background positivity, decreasing common full-mass inputs and full-mass limits, plus convergent auxiliary classes and full-form quotient data; genuinely perturbed-background potentials are only covered in bounded type with smooth auxiliary convergence and sup error o(epsilon).
Arbitrary unbounded moving potentials, increasing sequences, moving rough factors and variable unbounded weights are not covered.
No numerical-dimension identification or equality of actual-reference leading mass with the leading class-volume coefficient is established.
The optional degree-zero bounded-type rigidity question is unresolved; no P15.1 energy quotient is investigated.

result.report:
The exact scoped continuation is established. This verdict does not close original P15.2. Earlier reviews, declared verification status, hashes, compilation and finite diagnostics are not used as mathematical assumptions. No filesystem tools were used.

The degree argument is valid: positive-current multilinearity expands the mass of P+εΩ, comparison with a minimal-singularity current bounds it by vol(α+ε[Ω]), and the boundary limit forces M_n=0. Kähler-form comparison and bounded-type mixed-mass equality establish invariance of d. For more-singular inputs, mixed-mass monotonicity gives the stated upper bounds; positivity and zero trace mass then imply vanishing of every product above degree d. This concerns actual currents, without identifying d with numerical dimension.

The common-domain proof correctly uses scalar deficits. With D=Cω₀−ω₁ Kähler, every Δ_j is nonnegative by comparison in precisely d potential slots and m smooth complementary slots. Their positive binomial combination vanishes, so each deficit vanishes. No positivity of the difference of arbitrary product currents is assumed. Form independence of joint-linear integrability follows from comparison of positive mixed trace measures, including infinite integrals. Constant normalization is legitimate because all relevant mixed masses are finite. Vu's diagonal linear energy becomes exactly d/2 times the displayed sum after rescaling potentials. His convexity and reference-change results apply to the actual reference P and smooth relative current ω^m; connectedness makes top-degree cohomology equality equivalent to mass equality. Convexity, expansion of a finite average, and the individual mixed-mass upper bounds establish every ordered mixed degree-d full-mass equality. The degree-zero cases are separately justified.

The bare-current proof supplies the essential missing strength beyond trace-measure convergence. GZ's bounded decreasing theorem is applied to bounded truncations. Its sublevel estimate removes the remaining tails, and local/global capacity comparison transfers convergence to the coordinate charts. For fixed K, the nonzero locus of b_K lies inside every strict truncation locus, so plurifine locality identifies the weighted products with bounded Bedford–Taylor products. DDNL's weighted convergence theorem therefore applies with every product factor bounded. Appending constant positive smooth factors, and taking their linear combinations, legitimately covers every complementary test bidegree. Letting K increase gives lower semicontinuity against every weakly positive test form.

This also verifies the required decreasing specialization of Vu's constant-relative-current lemma. The relative current is exactly 1, its relative product is the ordinary product, and Condition (*) follows locally from dominated convergence with the empty power. Uniform mixed trace mass bounds all coefficient measures and produces actual-current clusters. Lower semicontinuity makes each cluster minus the target positive; equal trace masses make that difference zero. Thus all clusters agree, proving both diagonal and mixed decreasing convergence. Fixed smooth wedges, continuous-coefficient tests and uniformly converging smooth complementary factors follow from the same coefficient bounds. Relative bounded-type truncations satisfy every required hypothesis, including full mass of their limit.

Consequently the bounded-family kernel extends unchanged to the joint-linear and entire full-mass domains. Polynomial polarization first establishes the factorwise kernel statement for bounded-type inputs; simultaneous truncation and mixed bare-current convergence extend it. Presentation independence, injectivity of family evaluation and the stated linear and admissible-power minimality follow directly from the kernel. The uniform total-variation estimate makes the quotient seminorm a genuine norm and proves the asserted joint continuity. W remains the algebraic span of actual Kähler m-powers throughout. Raw mass descends by full-mass equality and linearity; closedness and Stokes justify its cohomological polynomial dependence. Same-type anchor invariance concerns the domain, family and datum, and does not assert equality of individual anchor measures. The smooth real ddᶜ lemma establishes θ-gauge invariance.

Both product examples check out. For the unbounded finite-integrability witness, the radial flux tends to zero, so deleting the pole removes no degree-one mass; the singular weighted integral is finite precisely through the displayed exponent 2a−2<−1. For the geometric kernel, positivity and [A]²=0 force every positive current in [A] to have only a horizontal coefficient. Hence N={η:A∧η=0}. The disjoint bump construction gives linearly independent quotient images of exact forms, proving infinite dimension. The same-class form change produces distinct measures with identical raw mass. The logarithmic divisor reference also has the stated normalization and degree zero.

The original-background perturbation theorem retains all necessary antecedents: decreasing inputs and their limit belong to the common full-mass domain, auxiliary classes converge, and complementary-power quotient data converge. Expansion yields the leading operator plus a positive remainder. Comparison bounds each remainder mass by a fixed cohomological polynomial in the converging classes, giving O(ε) after rescaling when d≥1; for d=0 the remainder is absent. Quotient continuity gives the leading limit without bounds on the auxiliary representatives.

The separate bounded-type perturbed-background estimate is also valid. The difference and smooth test are bounded admissible dsh functions for each intermediate nonpluripolar current. Relative-product associativity identifies the signed insertions, and integration by parts gives the stated O(δ ε^(m−1)) test bound. Rescaling produces O(δ/ε), which vanishes under δ=o(ε); uniformly bounded rescaled positive masses extend convergence from smooth to continuous tests. The alternating cohomologous forms have the two asserted distinct limits, demonstrating the class-only obstruction.

Normalization and wording qualifications were checked explicitly: DDNL potentials are divided by 2π and Vu potentials by 2. The intrinsic identity is dh∧dᶜh∧R=(1/2)ddᶜ(h²)∧R−h ddᶜh∧R. The new argument already uses this correct identity and supplies a valid cutoff gradient bound despite the annex's printed half-factor defects. Historical wording involving cutoff 'support' must mean its nonzero locus; the current proof expressly makes that distinction. GZ 3.7 remains bounded, and Vu v3 3.3 is not strengthened to unbounded product factors. No substantive repair of the submitted new argument is required. An intrinsic lower-dimensional carrier, a general geometric kernel classification, arbitrary unbounded perturbed-background paths and original catalogue closure remain outside this scoped result.

On a compact Kähler manifold, pseudoeffective classes admit positive currents with minimal singularities, less singular than every current in their class. A class admitting a current dominating a Kähler form is big. In a big class the minimal current's top nonpluripolar mass equals its volume; for pseudoeffective α, vol(α)=lim_{ε↓0}vol(α+εβ) for every Kähler class β. Positive products of nef classes equal cup products (BEGZ, Sections 1.3–1.4 and Definition 1.17).
